summary: Cameroon issues its visas through the official eVisa portal (evisacam.cm) — you apply online and the approved visa is issued on arrival or at an embassy — but the portal does not list which nationalities are exempt; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens need a visa. Citizens of fellow CEMAC states (Chad, CAR, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea) enter visa-free under the Community’s free-movement act.

notes: The UK government's travel advice says it is illegal to buy, sell, kill or capture any protected wild animal or trade its parts without a licence, and that offenders can be prosecuted and imprisoned or fined.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Cameroon is largely a cash-based economy and that credit cards are rarely accepted outside international hotels. The UK government says shops usually want small notes, which can be hard to get, that ATMs are not often available outside large towns, and that euros and US dollars are the most widely accepted foreign currencies.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all travel to the Far-North Region (except around Maroua), the North-West and South-West regions (except Limbé), the Bakassi Peninsula and within 40 km of the borders with Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic. It says terrorist attacks could occur anywhere, including Yaoundé and Douala, and that there is a risk of armed robbery and mugging throughout the country; Canada says violent crime occurs frequently, especially at night, in major cities and on main roads.

tips.text: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to the North-West and South-West regions and the Far North. The UK makes exceptions around Maroua and advises against all but essential travel to Limbé, and also against all travel to the Bakassi Peninsula and within 40 km of the borders with Nigeria (except Garoua), Chad and the Central African Republic.
Cameroon's consular portal says visa applications can only be made online at evisacam.cm. Once approved, the visa is affixed at the entry border post or at a Cameroonian embassy or consulate.

Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required of every traveller aged 1 year or over, according to the WHO country list, and Cameroon's visa portal lists international vaccination certificates among the documents for every visa category.

The UK government's travel advice says to avoid travelling at night, particularly in rural areas, as many roads are unlit and in poor condition, and that police and gendarmerie roadblocks are common. It also says to always carry ID — a residence permit or a certified copy of your passport showing a valid visa — and that police can detain you without it.

The UK government's travel advice says shops usually want small notes, which can be hard to obtain, that ATMs are not often available outside large towns, and that euros and US dollars are the most widely accepted foreign currencies.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cameroon?
faq.answer: Citizens of the CEMAC bloc (Chad, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea) enter visa-free. For other nationalities, Cameroon’s eVisa portal says to apply online unless your visa is waived, but it does not list the waived nationalities; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens need a visa. Travellers who need one apply in advance on evisacam.cm and receive the visa on arrival or at an embassy.

faq.question: Does Cameroon offer a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Not without prior approval. You must apply and be approved on evisacam.cm before traveling; the visa sticker is then affixed at the airport or border post when you enter, or at a Cameroonian embassy or consulate.

faq.question: How much does the Cameroon eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The online processing fee is 153 EUR for a short-stay visa (1 to 180 days), 229 EUR for an express short-stay visa, 305 EUR for a long-stay visa (181 to 360 days) and 153 EUR for a transit visa. It is paid on evisacam.cm and is not refunded if the visa is refused.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Cameroon?
faq.answer: Yes — proof of yellow fever vaccination is required for all travellers aged 1 year or over, regardless of where they are arriving from.

faq.question: Is Cameroon safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Parts of it are not. The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to the North-West, South-West and Far North regions; the UK advises against all but essential travel to Limbé and the North Region, including Garoua. Canada says violent crime occurs frequently, especially at night, in major cities and on main roads.
